title: Interactive Academic Discussion Protocol Map
description: Understand (L2 — Understand) the structure and participant roles of four major academic discussion protocols by interactively exploring their differences.
creator: English Language Arts
subject: English Language Arts
Speaking and Listening

learningObjectives: Describe the participant structure, facilitator role, evidence requirements, learning goal, and typical duration of a Socratic seminar, a fishbowl, philosophical chairs, and numbered heads together.
Compare one attribute across all four discussion protocols.
Identify the responsibilities of a facilitator, inner-circle member, outer-circle member, or small group member in a given protocol.
Select sentence frames appropriate to a role when preparing for a discussion.
educational.prerequisites: The descriptions of the four discussion protocols and the sentence frames of academic discussion in Chapter 14.

pedagogical.modelType: click-to-explore concept network with a comparison panel and a role preparation card
pedagogical.assessment: Readers match each protocol to its participant structure, explain how the facilitator role differs between two protocols, and complete two sentence frames for their own role.
misconceptionsAddressed: All class discussions follow the same rules.
The facilitator's job is to supply answers.
Observers in a fishbowl have nothing to do until it is their turn to speak.

controls.label: Explore
controls.action: shows the protocol map and the detail or comparison panel

controls.label: Protocol node
controls.action: focuses one protocol and lists its five attributes in full

controls.label: Attribute node
controls.action: highlights that attribute under all four protocols and compares them in the panel
